ULTI-MAT-S / ULTI-MAT-B: Evac+Chair Ulti-Mat Evacuation Sled for Stairs
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/evac-chair-ulti-mat-s-ultimat-b
Manufacturer page: https://evac-chair.com/ulti-mat/
Spec sheet: Evac+Chair range brochure
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: evacuation sled for stairs (40/mo, KD0). Secondary: evacuation mat (10), evacuation mattress (10), patient evacuation mat (0). Ricky's note: rescue sled (100) is used on the Evac+Sled page, so it is not repeated here.
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Evac+Chair Ulti-Mat Evacuation Sled for Stairs in Standard and Bariatric Sizes – ULTI-MAT-S / ULTI-MAT-B
Current H1: Evac+Chair ULTI-MAT Ulti-Mat Evacuation Sled
Subtitle: Padded Patient Evacuation Mat with a 660 lb or 1,000 lb Capacity for Two-Person Roll-and-Drag Evacuation Down Stairs
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair ULTI-MAT Ulti-Mat Evacuation Sled
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair Ulti-Mat is an evacuation sled for stairs that lets two staff members move a person with limited mobility out of a building quickly and safely in an emergency. The person lies on the mat, which wraps around them, and the staff pull it along the floor and down the stairs with no lifting, using a roll and drag method that lets carers move patients 2 to 3 times their own weight.
Made from highly durable fabric over a foam pad, this patient evacuation mat cushions the body like a padded mini mattress. A single piece of strong webbing runs the full length of the mat and forms the head and foot pulling straps, and side wings fold over the passenger before the straps and buckles are fastened. When it is not needed, the Ulti-Mat rolls up into its own foot pocket for compact storage, in standard and bariatric sizes.
Operation: Two people; roll and drag method, with no lifting
Construction: Highly durable fabric with a foam pad, and a padded mini mattress under the body for comfort
Webbing: A single piece of strong webbing runs the full length of the mat, forming the head and foot pulling straps
Pulling Straps: Long pulling straps at the head and feet, so several people can help
Body Protection: Side wings wrap around the passenger and enclose the legs and arms, with the option of leaving the arms out
Straps: Two body straps for tall and short patients, a leg strap, and two securing cross straps, with heavy duty strap clips; the straps adjust to fit patients of all sizes
Carrying Handles: Four high-visibility yellow carrying handles on the base
Use: Rolls out for vertical (stairs) and horizontal evacuation, and moves easily over virtually any surface; narrow and flexible
Compatibility: Can be used with a backboard or basket stretcher
Storage: Rolls up into its self-contained foot pocket, which doubles as a carry bag
Weight Capacity: 660 lbs typical safe working load (standard) or 1,000 lbs (bariatric); both sizes tested to 1,500 lbs
Size Unrolled: 78.7”L×47.3”W×1”D
Size Packed: 21.2”W×9.4”D×8.6”H
Weight: 9 lbs
Warranty: 2-year manufacturer’s warranty
Available Models and Options
ULTI-MAT-S – Standard: 660 lb typical safe working load, tested to 1,500 lbs
ULTI-MAT-B – Bariatric: 1,000 lb typical safe working load, tested to 1,500 lbs
[H2] Applications
The Ulti-Mat suits buildings where people who cannot walk, or cannot be moved into an evacuation chair, may need to be taken down the stairs in an emergency.
Typical applications include:
Hospitals, nursing homes, senior living, and care facilities
Bariatric care, with the 1,000 lb bariatric size
Schools, offices, hotels, and high-rise buildings, as part of an emergency evacuation plan
Horizontal evacuation along corridors to a safe area on the same floor
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
How does an evacuation sled for stairs work?
The person is placed on the Ulti-Mat, the side wings are wrapped around them, and the straps are fastened. Two staff members then pull the mat by its head and foot straps, sliding it across the floor and down the stairs without lifting the person.
How many people does it take to use the Ulti-Mat?
Two. The long pulling straps at the head and feet let more people help when needed.
What is the difference between the standard and bariatric Ulti-Mat?
The standard ULTI-MAT-S has a typical safe working load of 660 lbs, and the bariatric ULTI-MAT-B has a typical safe working load of 1,000 lbs. Both are tested to 1,500 lbs.
When should I choose an evacuation mat instead of an evacuation chair?
An evacuation chair carries the person sitting up. An evacuation mat like the Ulti-Mat carries the person lying down, so it suits people who are bedbound or cannot be moved into a chair.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: the primary keyword "evacuation sled for stairs" is in the H1, first sentence, an FAQ question, the meta title, and the meta description. The secondary keywords are used where they read naturally: "patient evacuation mat" (subtitle and second intro paragraph), "evacuation mat" (FAQ), and "mattress" ("padded mini mattress," the Evac+Chair wording). As Ricky noted, "rescue sled" stays on the Evac+Sled page, so it is not used here.
Research: the search results for "evacuation sled for stairs" are mostly sled makers (Med Sled) and stores that put the capacity and size in the product name (Global Industrial and Zoro sell this Ulti-Mat as "Evacuation Sled, 660 lb Capacity"). So the subtitle has both capacities, and the FAQs answer how the sled works, how many people it takes, standard vs. bariatric, and when to choose a mat instead of a chair.
Data sheet: the "ULTI-MAT DATA SHEET" button on the Evac+Chair web page opens the data sheet for a different product (ResQMat, 89” x 51”). The real Ulti-Mat data sheet (an Evac+Chair PDF, hosted by Rehabmart) has the same text as the web page, so I used the web page and the range brochure as sources.
Warranty: the Ulti-Mat data sheet says "2 year manufacturer's warranty." Our current page says "Ask about their lifetime warranty," but that is the chair warranty. I used 2 years.
Size and weight: Evac+Chair gives one size (78.7” x 47.3” unrolled, 9 lbs). It does not say whether this is the standard or bariatric size, and gives no size for the bariatric mat. Do you know the bariatric size and weight? If not, should I label these as the standard size?
Left out: "World's No.1," "Successful in saving lives in 9/11," and the lifetime warranty line from our current page.
Duplicate content: our current description is the Evac+Chair text word for word. The new copy is fully rewritten.
H1: the current H1 repeats the name ("ULTI-MAT Ulti-Mat"). The new H1 ends with the two model codes from our variants, ULTI-MAT-S and ULTI-MAT-B.
Images: the 4 current Evac+Chair images are kept (all have the alt text "Evac+Chair ULTI-MAT-S Ulti-Mat Standard"). I did not find a bariatric photo on the Evac+Chair website.
Shipping weight: both variants are set to 200 lbs; the mat weighs 9 lbs. Is 200 lbs a placeholder?
Price: $645 / $860 (standard) and $1,150 / $1,533 (bariatric), both 75% of compare-at. No change made.
Current meta description is the general GSA pricing line. GSA is not mentioned in the description, per your note on the other tabs.
